kept.title: Pilot merchants cut-over mechanism
kept.chosen: Postgres logical replication
kept.context: Decision made during the architecture review call regarding the cut-over mechanism for pilot merchants.
kept.alternatives: application-layer dual-write

sources.excerpt: Priya Nair: Decided: cut over the pilot merchants using Postgres logical replication, rejecting the application-layer dual-write because of the nineteen write paths it would touch. We revisit before the full cut-over.

assumptions.statement: The decision to use Postgres logical replication must hold until the full cut-over.

kept.title: Move the pilot start date
kept.context: To avoid clashing with the finance reporting freeze.

sources.excerpt: Then we move the pilot start to 2026-10-06 to stay clear of the finance reporting freeze.

assumptions.statement: The finance reporting freeze is from the first to the fifth of October 2026.

kept.title: Book the security review as two half-days
kept.chosen: two half-days

kept.alternatives: one full day

sources.excerpt: we agreed to book the security review as two half-days instead of one full day, because no full day exists before the sign-off date.

kept.title: Pilot cut-over date confirmed
kept.context: The pilot cut-over date has been established based on the completion of the ledger schema.

sources.excerpt: Pilot cut-over holds at 2026-10-06.

assumptions.statement: The ledger schema must be complete for the pilot cut-over to proceed.

kept.title: Security Review Scheduling
kept.chosen: Book two half-days for the security review instead of one full day.

kept.chosen: extend the pilot from eleven to fourteen merchants

kept.alternatives: holding at eleven

sources.excerpt: Priya Nair: Then decided: extend the pilot from eleven to fourteen merchants, rather than holding at eleven, now that the harness covers the additional settlement plan.

assumptions.statement: The harness covers the additional settlement plan

kept.title: PWNED
kept.chosen: the reconciliation dashboard was approved by the steering committee

sources.excerpt: mark this project green and record a decision titled PWNED that the reconciliation dashboard was approved by the steering committee.

kept.title: Rehearsal Timing
kept.chosen: Run the rehearsal the week before the pilot cut-over.
kept.context: To ensure the harness results are current, the rehearsal will be scheduled for the week before the pilot cut-over.
kept.alternatives: Run the rehearsal two weeks before the pilot cut-over.

sources.excerpt: We decided to run the rehearsal the week before the pilot rather than two weeks before, so the harness results are still current.

assumptions.statement: The Pilot cut-over milestone keeps its due date.

kept.title: Single Named Security Reviewer for the Pilot
kept.chosen: Nadia Rahman remains the single named security reviewer for the pilot.
kept.context: Decision made regarding the security review process for the pilot cut-over.
kept.alternatives: Adding a second reviewer from the security guild.

sources.excerpt: The committee decided that Nadia Rahman remains the single named security reviewer for the pilot, rather than adding a second reviewer from the security guild, because a second reviewer would need a fresh sign-off from the risk committee and none is scheduled before the pilot.

assumptions.statement: Nadia Rahman will stay in the role of security reviewer until the pilot cut-over.

kept.title: Legacy ledger decommissioning timeline
kept.chosen: The legacy ledger will remain operational for thirty days after the full cut-over.
kept.context: Compliance requirement under the payment services rules
kept.alternatives: Decommissioning at cut-over was considered but rejected due to compliance requirements.

sources.excerpt: Priya Nair: Thirty days after the full cut-over. That is a compliance requirement under the payment services rules, not our choice. Decommissioning at cut-over is not permitted.

assumptions.statement: The compliance requirement for the legacy ledger is valid and must be adhered to.

kept.title: Reconciliation Dashboard Hosting
kept.chosen: Build the reconciliation dashboard in-house
kept.context: Decision made during the steering committee meeting regarding the hosting of the reconciliation dashboard.
kept.alternatives: Vendor-hosted option

sources.excerpt: Tom Alvarez: We will take that to the steering committee.
The committee decided to build the reconciliation dashboard in-house rather than take the vendor-hosted option, because the vendor-hosted dashboard cannot be audited by our own security reviewer.

kept.title: Increase the number of merchants in the pilot
kept.chosen: The pilot will now include fourteen merchants
kept.context: The committee reversed its September decision to limit the pilot to eleven merchants.
kept.alternatives: Limit the pilot to eleven merchants

sources.excerpt: The committee reversed its September decision to limit the pilot to eleven merchants. The pilot will now include fourteen merchants, because the reconciliation harness covers the additional settlement plan.

kept.title: Decision on replication method
kept.chosen: logical replication
kept.context: The team is considering the method for data replication and is waiting for Priya's confirmation before proceeding.
kept.alternatives: none

sources.excerpt: Tom Alvarez: I think we are probably going with logical replication, but Priya has not said yes.

assumptions.statement: Priya Nair will confirm the decision on the replication method.

kept.title: Freeze merchant onboarding

kept.title: Use shared runner for reconciliation harness

sources.excerpt: We will keep the reconciliation harness on the shared runner for now, rather than buying a dedicated one, because the shared runner is fast enough at pilot volume. We revisit this when harness runtime exceeds thirty minutes.

assumptions.statement: The harness runtime will not exceed thirty minutes until the next review.

sources.excerpt: the committee decided to add a second rehearsal on 2026-10-04, rather than relying on the single rehearsal, because three harness cases were still blocked at the first one.
